title: Symmetry of integration of even Tate-line products
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$ for arbitrary $n\geq1$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$. Write $p_m:X_m=\mathbf A^m_Y\to Y$, $T_m=A_{X_m}(m)[2m]$, $V_m=Rp_{m!}T_m$ for $m\geq1$ [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Put $U=V_1$ and let $t_Y:U\to A_Y$ be the normalized integration [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. Use the concrete finite constant-$A$ pro-etale compact-support, exchange and projection maps [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], [def-exchange-projection], and their canonical composition comparisons. Suppose $U\cong A_Y$, and suppose every $V_m$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude and every canonical relative-product map
$$\kappa_{m,1}:V_{m+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_m\otimes_A^LU$$
is invertible. This map means the specific inverse of the forward compact-support product (the displayed construction in [thm-sf-kunneth-relative]), not an arbitrary isomorphism between these objects. Set $\kappa_1=1_U$ and $\kappa_{m+1}=(\kappa_m\otimes1_U)\kappa_{m,1}$. Suppose given maps $J_m:V_m\to A_Y$ with $J_1=t_Y$ and $J_{m+1}=(J_m\otimes t_Y)\kappa_{m,1}$, with tensor-unit constraints understood.
Then $J_m=t_Y^{\otimes m}\kappa_m$. For a coordinate permutation $s_\sigma:X_m\xrightarrow{\sim}X_m$, let $S_\sigma:V_m\xrightarrow{\sim}V_m$ be the map induced by that scheme isomorphism and its pullback on $T_m$, identified with $T_m$ using twist additivity. The concrete $\kappa_m$ are compatible with reassociation and permutations on these finite-Tor inputs: every parenthesization of the iterated relative product $V_m\to U^{\otimes_A^Lm}$ formed from the same specified maps equals $\kappa_m$ after the derived-tensor associators, and $\kappa_m\circ S_\sigma=P_\sigma\circ\kappa_m$, where $P_\sigma$ permutes the factors of $U^{\otimes_A^Lm}$ by the signed symmetry of derived tensor. Moreover
$$J_m\circ S_\sigma=J_m.$$
Here the signed external-tensor interchange of two coordinate Tate lines agrees with the untwisted coordinate identification: on $A(1)[2]$ the sign is $(-1)^{(-2)(-2)}=1$, and on blocks of lengths $d,e$ it is $(-1)^{(-2d)(-2e)}=1$. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, the induced coordinate permutation also preserves $(1_K\otimes J_m)\Pi_{m,K}:Rp_{m!}(Lp_m^*K\otimes^LT_m)\to K$, where $\Pi_{m,K}$ is the inverse projection map with $K$ first. No six-functor datum with a duality axiom, exceptional-purity theorem, or coordinate invariance hypothesis is an input.

proof.text: Induct on r using the given recursion for J and the definitions of kappa and powerTrace. The successor step is tensor functoriality: tensor of a composite equals the composite of tensor maps. This is tensorPowerRecursion in Lean.

Apply the concrete binary normalization equation. Induct on ProductTree: the leaf is the identity; the join is the tensor of the two induction hypotheses followed by forward. Tensor functoriality and binary normalization give exactly the recursive tree normalize followed by kappa inverse. Both factors are isomorphisms, so treeForward is invertible.

The canonical signed braiding of U with itself is the identity because U is isomorphic to the tensor unit. By braiding naturality it suffices to check the unit, where braiding followed by the left unitor is the right unitor and the two unitors coincide by monoidal coherence. Induct in the explicit lastAdjacent, lastSwap and permutation recursions: every adjacent interchange is the identity and each conjugation is therefore the identity. Apply coordinateIntertwining and cancel kappa to get coordinateAction=id. This proves its invertibility and fixes every J_r, without assuming the trace is an isomorphism.

Apply evenTateLineSelfSymmetry and the same recursive identity-permutation argument. Functoriality of inverse image and the right identity law prove the coordinateTate equation. The integer scalar identity follows by rewriting the exponent as 2 times d*(2*e) and applying pow_mul with (-1)^2=1.

Use coefficientProjectionNaturality and coordinateAction=id. Tensoring two identities is the identity, so the invertible forward projection followed by coefficientAction equals itself. Cancel the projection, using projection_isIso, to obtain coefficientAction=id. It therefore fixes coefficientTrace for the supplied J.
